target_customer: HR, people analytics, IT and leadership teams at mid and large companies
problem: Employee engagement surveys are repetitive and slow, so leaders lacked a continuous view of how teams collaborate.

founders.name: Philip Arkcoll
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC and as CEO on the company about page. TechCrunch spells the name Phillip.

founders.name: Erik Schultink
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch March 2018 and as CTO on the about page. TechCrunch says the pair drew on experience scaling companies but names no employers.

competitors.name: Microsoft Workplace Analytics
competitors.what: Analytics on Office 365 collaboration data for managers

competitors.name: StatusToday
competitors.what: Startup with a similar approach to analyzing workplace collaboration

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting a few dozen apps, anonymizing data and computing collaboration metrics is standard integration engineering with privacy design challenges.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and a privacy proxy help, but Microsoft owned the data in its own suite and rivals could copy analytics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft offered Workplace Analytics and later Viva Insights for its own data; Worklytics remained independent and positions around many tools beyond Microsoft.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2018 framed the pain as lame meetings and inefficient teams. Survey fatigue was the stated gap. No customer figures at the time were found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and results focused; stresses privacy and anonymity

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive work plus analytics coinage with a .co domain. No press on the brand itself was found, though it lists customers such as Uber and Pinterest as logos.

pivots.to: AI spend tracking and ROI measurement across tools
pivots.why: Current site focuses on AI adoption and spend; timing not stated

outcome_analysis: Worklytics launched out of the Winter 2018 batch with passive collaboration analytics and no found Series A or acquisition. It remains small, with an aggregator showing only a tiny seed, yet it has grown a customer list including Uber, Pinterest and Asana and now targets AI spend measurement. Funding is unknown, so its trajectory is not clearly success or stall.
notes: Unverified: CB Insights lists a 120 thousand dollar seed on 2018-03-09 with Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund and Bowery Capital; single aggregator so not recorded as a round. Founding year 2015 per CB Insights, 2016 per YC. Founder education and prior employers not found. Completeness pass: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights); Persana dates a seed 2018-02-04 with no amount, and Bowery Capital appears only on CB Insights.
